title: Dutch eyewear chain Hans Anders halts sale of Meta glasses, citing privacy concerns
key_facts: Hans Anders, a large Dutch eyewear chain (parent company Nexeye), is pausing sales of Meta glasses; Dutch online retailer Wehkamp is also pausing sales.
A Nexeye spokesperson said the decision follows the ongoing public and political debate and that Hans Anders will await the outcome before deciding whether to offer them again.
The halt follows a story in the Dutch newspaper AD about people, especially women, being secretly filmed in public.
Meta says each camera pair has a bright light that blinks when recording, cannot be turned off, and the camera is disabled if covered or tampered with.

The Dutch Data Protection Authority has warned about camera glasses and is investigating further measures; the nonprofit Offlimits urged Meta and EssilorLuxottica to pull them; in September the consumer group Consumentenbond urged a ban.

The Dutch government is not rushing a ban: state secretary for justice Claudia van Bruggen said the Data Protection Authority had only six reports and one complaint, and the government awaits a European Data Protection Board report due later this year.
quote_evidence: At least two Dutch retailers are pausing the sale of the glasses following media reports about privacy concerns, and the government is also getting involved.
The sales halt comes after a Dutch newspaper, AD, published a story about people, especially women, being surreptitiously filmed in public.
However, the Dutch government isn't rushing to enact a ban.
why_it_matters_hint: Retailers are stopping sales of camera glasses over fears of secret filming, while the government waits for more evidence.
event_date: 2 Oct 2026 (Hans Anders pause announced; other outlets dated 2 Oct 2026)
